text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have been experiencing fever and altered mentation for the past two days. To help me assess your condition, can you tell me your age and if you have any history of recent travel or tick bites?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Given your history of taking haloperidol, I need to check for signs of Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome; can you describe if you have experienced any muscle rigidity or involuntary movements recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text: You are describing classic signs of Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome, but I must rule out infection. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, Creatine Kinase, Electrolytes
